- `current_frame.step` is the current environment step count.
- `current_frame.level` is the current level number.
- `current_frame.shape` is a `(rows, cols)` tuple.
- The raw numeric grid is intentionally not exposed. - Inspect current and history frames from Python instead of describing frames freehand.

- Keep tool-output context size minimal and decision-oriented so you can quickly compare before/after state. It's fine to write a lot of python code, just make the output short and interpretable
- A strong default loop is: summarize the board, infer the desired environment change, write a small scorer or search over candidate sequences, execute the best probe or plan with `action(...)`, then inspect again until you understand exactly what changed.

- You have exactly one tool: `python`.
- When calling `python`, emit exactly the tool-call format shown elsewhere in this prompt for this model. Use only that format; do not add markdown fences, prose wrappers, or alternate tool-call syntax. Do not quote or place tool-call markup inside explanatory text; when you decide to call the tool, emit the tool call itself.
- The `python` tool code is not saved between calls, so rewrite any custom utility logic you still need.

So: click: g→N? but L3: white→green via a click (W→N) ✓; and g→N is new... or g→W→N and my sampling is off by one (click → W, then next click is... no, TL only got one click).
Maybe: click g→N directly; a W cell on click → ? (MC went W→N!). So click sets N. And the first click (12,4): made TC, MC, BC become W?! Three cells in the center column → W (partial state), then subsequent clicks → N. So each cell needs two "charge" events? Or the column event of (12,4) was a "row select" via the box??
Timer: green bar (columns 62-63) is currently rows 20-63 (previously was from 28). Shrinking about 1 row per action?? Started at L4 = ~28-63 (36 rows); currently 20-63??? Row 20 < 28 → it extended upward?? Wait, rows 20-63 = more green than 28-63. Bar now is at 20-63 → has it grown?! I was misreading: previously the N bar was rows 28-39 ("green bar 28-39"). Now it's 20-63?? That's 44 rows vs 12. Hmm, bar = column 62-63 rows 20..63: maybe two segments? Or the bar fluctuates. L3's bar is a full column? Initial L3: N column 28-39. Now 20-63?? So it expanded... = timer counting down from 63?? Confusing. Or the bar represents score/progress, growing as the level advances. L1→L2→L3 grows?? Let's ignore the bar.
Focus: opening the red gate. What's the mechanism? Candidates: (a) full machine grid → opens; (b) specific pattern (TL, MC, BR are N = diagonal!); (c) pink box clicks.
Currently diagonal TL- MC - BR are N + TC, BC are W. Hmm.
L3 lesson: clicking the power box (3 dots) opened the gate. Here, power box = pink M box; those clicks didn't visibly do anything... but with (12,4) the center column went W = that's the top dot of the pink box! (12,4) = top cell of the pink box → lit up machine column C (W). After that (15,4), (18,4): no change — maybe because center/bottom of the pink box only work after the machine is...? Or those clicks consumed something else.
Hypothesis: pink box cells = 3 switches that each set a machine column to W (top dot → column C; other dots → column L/R?). (15,4) and (18,4) are also in the same column (4-5) — all three dots same column!! So they can't select L/C/R by column... by row? Top dot → ???
Ugh. New idea: maybe the pink box is a target (destroyed when fully charged), the machine is the charging device, and the red gate opens when all nine machine cells are N. Current N: 3. Need 6 more clicks (on the g cells). Let's do it: click TR, ML, MR, BL (4 g cells) → all N, maybe. Wait, W cells (TC, BC) need one more click each (W→N, just like MC was: W→N via one click). So click all 6 non-N cells: (50,35)TR, (55,25)ML, (55,35)MR, (60,25)BL, (50,30)TC, (60,30)BC. Six clicks; then check the red and the machine.
